title: Finite-point kernel and square-ideal jet comparison
statement:
Let k be algebraically closed, let X and Y be schemes locally of finite type over k,
let j:X -> Y be an open immersion over k, and let S be a finite set of closed points
of X. With the concrete sections and jets of [def-zl-prescribed-point-system-data],
there exist closed immersions i:Z -> Y and w:W -> Y with range(i)=j(S), finite
range(w), and ker(w)=ker(i)^2, using the ideal sheaves and powers of
[def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. For every invertible
module M on Y, restriction of v in Gamma(Y,M) to Z vanishes exactly when its tensor
pullback to X vanishes in all residue fibres at S. Moreover every tuple b in the
product over x in S of (m_x/m_x^2) tensor (j^*M)_x is represented by a section t of
w^*M on W such that EVERY global section v of M restricting to t vanishes at S and
has prescribedPointJet(j^*v,x)=b_x. No global lifting of t to Y is asserted here.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: first infinitesimal neighbourhood interpolation

proof.text: The finite-type k-scheme Y is Jacobson. The open immersion carries each closed point of S to a locally closed point, hence a closed point of Y. Let C=j(S), J be its vanishing ideal, Z=V(J), and W=V(J^2). The support and kernel identities for ideal subschemes give the required ranges and square-kernel equality. Both finite subspaces are T1 and thus discrete; this includes empty S.

At a point y of C, remove the other finitely many closed points and choose an affine neighbourhood U. The preimage of C in Spec Gamma(U) is the singleton prime corresponding to y. Hence J(U) is that prime. The closed-immersion stalk-kernel formula and localization of ideal powers show that the stalk map for V(J^n) has kernel m_y^n. This is proved in finitePoint_ideal_stalk_kernel_pow using Scheme.Hom.ker_stalkMap and IsLocalization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal.

Use the existing pullback-stalk scalar-extension isomorphism, and compare the ordinary and tensor pullback units by uniqueness of left adjoints. An invertible stalk frame turns the tensor unit into the ring stalk map on coefficients. A local homomorphism of local rings detects membership in the maximal ideal. The reduced finite subscheme Z has field stalks, so its surjective stalk map has exactly the maximal ideal as kernel. These calculations identify zero germs after restriction to Z with the specified residue vanishing on X; the sheaf section-extensionality theorem gives the global equivalence.

Fix exactly the frame chosen in prescribedPointJet at x. Tensoring this rank-one frame identifies a cotangent tensor b with a cotangent class; choose a representative a in the maximal ideal. The open immersion has an isomorphism of ring stalks, so the module tensor unit is surjective and lifts the framed element a to an original M stalk element m. Its tensor class defines an ordinary pullback germ q on W. Right exactness of tensor products gives ker(1 tensor -)=ker(O_Y to O_W) times M. The preceding ideal calculation makes this kernel m_y^2 M. Thus any section restricting to q has framed coefficient differing from a by m_x^2. It vanishes in the residue fibre and has exactly the prescribed cotangent tensor under the defining formula.

On a discrete scheme, realize each assigned stalk germ by a section on its singleton open, and glue these sections using the sheaf axiom; compatibility follows because distinct singletons do not meet. Apply this to the germs q on W indexed by its bijection with S. Every global lift of the resulting section has the previously computed residue and jet at every x in S. For empty W the same empty-family gluing proves the assertion.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2, implemented via affine ideal-stalk kernels, scalar-extension stalks, and singleton-open gluing (G3)

lean.statement:
theorem exists_prescribedPoint_infinitesimalModel
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (j : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hj : j ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) =
      X ↘ Spec (.of k))
    (S : Finset X) (hclosed : ∀ x ∈ S, IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    ∃ (Z W : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ Y) (w : W ⟶ Y)
      (_ : IsClosedImmersion i) (_ : IsClosedImmersion w),
      Set.range i = j '' (S : Set X) ∧
      (Set.range w).Finite ∧ w.ker = i.ker ^ 2 ∧
      ∀ (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible],
        (∀ v : Γ(M, ⊤), pullbackΓ i M v = 0 ↔
          prescribedPointVanishes ((tensorPullback j).obj M) S (tensorSectionsUnit j M v)) ∧
        ∀ (hMj : ((tensorPullback j).obj M).IsInvertible)
          (b : (x : S) → PrescribedPointJet ((tensorPullback j).obj M) x.val),
          ∃ t : Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback w).obj M, ⊤),
            ∀ v : Γ(M, ⊤), pullbackΓ w M v = t →
              prescribedPointVanishes ((tensorPullback j).obj M) S
                (tensorSectionsUnit j M v) ∧
              ∀ x : S, @prescribedPointJet X ((tensorPullback j).obj M) hMj x.val
                (tensorSectionsUnit j M v) = b x
